items.question: Is the nanosatellite/CubeSat mission context and lifecycle stage described clearly enough to interpret applicability?

quality_checklist.overall_rationale: The study is relevant and fairly transparent about a CubeSat budget-calculation MBSE proof of concept, with executable OPCloud/OPM artifacts and example component data. Quality is limited by missing venue details in the markdown, generic mission context, absence of full model/code availability, and lack of empirical outcome metrics, flight data, or formal requirements traceability.

bibliographic_review_management.status_rationale: Retained as supporting: the full text presents an MBSE/OPM executable CubeSat budget-calculation model that includes power budget and EPS attributes, but it is not primarily an EPS architecture, EPS behavior, or mission-level verification study.
bibliographic_review_management.citation: Jbara, A. (2025). Applying Model-Based Systems Engineering on CubeSat Budget Calculating. DOI: 10.1109/aero63441.2025.11068482.
bibliographic_review_management.title: Applying Model-Based Systems Engineering on CubeSat Budget Calculating

RQ1.rationale: The paper models a generic CubeSat as OPM objects/processes with four subsystems including EPS and budget attributes, using minimal OPM constructs and OPL; however, it does not provide a general behavioral mission/EPS model.

RQ2.rationale: It claims reliability/compatibility, consistency, standardization, and automation benefits from MBSE-enabled budget screening, but these outcomes are system-level and asserted or demonstrated only via a budget example, not EPS-specific evidence.

RQ3.rationale: It integrates pre-physical verification as executable model calculations, thresholds, and accepted/error states, with EPS contributing power/mass/size inputs; it does not define EPS-specific V&V procedures or hardware tests.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: No previous extraction, corpus file, sources.bib, or other paper was read. Within the paper, related work contrasts the OPM/OPCloud approach with a Matlab budget-calculation thesis and Excel-based tools, but lineage overlap for this SLR was not checked due to silo rules.

RQ1: A generic CubeSat is modeled in OPM as a system with subsystems including EPS, OBC, TRXVU, and Antenna System, each represented mostly through mass, dimensional, and power attributes.
The paper supports minimal-knowledge modeling through OPM's small set of objects/processes/states, generated OPL, and budget formulas rather than detailed subsystem behavioral models.
EPS is included as a parameterized subsystem and input to system budgets, not as a detailed electrical power architecture or behavioral EPS model.
RQ2: Claimed MBSE outcomes include rapid screening for reliable/compatible component selection, process clarity, automation, consistency/synchronization, standardization, and stakeholder comprehensibility.

Evidence for outcomes is strongest for executable calculation/accept-reject demonstration and weak for reliability, reproducibility, integrability, and ROI because no measured outcomes or independent validation are provided.
Reproducibility is partial: diagrams, values, and a code snippet are present, but no full model/code package is reported.
RQ3: Verification is integrated into the model through executable budget calculations, threshold checks, Error outputs, and Component Selection state changes before physical build.
The demonstration uses real ISISPACE subsystem data and an altered-data failure case, providing moderate evidence for system-level budget verification.
The verification is not EPS-specific beyond EPS attribute participation in mass, volume, height, and power budgets; no EPS test procedures or hardware validation are reported.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: "However, this work is not meant to be comprehensive in this regard, but rather to use some of the budget calculations to demonstrate a tool that automates the process of budget calculation."
"These are the very basic input/output mechanisms, but there are more advanced methods, but these are beyond the scope of this work."
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No named mission, payload, orbit, or mission-domain scenario is reported.
EPS is reduced to dimensional, mass, and power attributes; no EPS modes, solar array, battery, regulation, load profile, or interface behavior is modeled in detail.
Full OPCloud model, complete JavaScript code, and reusable data package are not provided.
No empirical baseline, reliability metric, stakeholder evaluation, integration test, hardware-in-the-loop result, or flight data is reported.
Formal requirements traceability and lifecycle review gates are not implemented beyond budget thresholds and the component-selection state.
